passages.text: Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, “Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. And now his creditor is coming to take my two children as his slaves!”
passages.sermon:
A woman was the wife of one of the sons of the prophets.
She cried out to Elisha.
She said, “My husband, your servant, is dead.
You know that your servant feared the LORD.
Now a creditor is coming.
He wants to take my two children as his slaves.”
passages.original: וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־ הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה אֶל־ אֱלִישָׁ֜ע לֵאמֹ֗ר עַבְדְּךָ֤ אִישִׁי֙ מֵ֔ת וְאַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּ֣י עַבְדְּךָ֔ הָיָ֥ה יָרֵ֖א אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה וְהַ֨נֹּשֶׁ֔ה בָּ֗א לָקַ֜חַת אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֧י יְלָדַ֛י ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

passages.text: “How can I help you?” asked Elisha. “Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She answered, “Your servant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
A woman came to Elisha for help.
Elisha spoke to the woman.
Elisha said, “How can I help you?”
Elisha asked, “Tell me what you have in your house.”
The woman answered Elisha.
She said, “Your servant has nothing in the house.”
She said, “I have only a jar of oil.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֤יהָ אֱלִישָׁע֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לָּ֔ךְ הַגִּ֣ידִי לִ֔י מַה־ יֶּשׁ־ לְכִי בַּבָּ֑יִת וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֣ין לְשִׁפְחָתְךָ֥ כֹל֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת כִּ֖י אִם־ אָס֥וּךְ שָֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: “Go,” said Elisha, “borrow jars, even empty ones, from all your neighbors. Do not gather just a few.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha spoke to the woman.
Elisha said, “Go.
Borrow jars from outside your house.
Ask all your neighbors for jars.
Get empty jars.
Do not gather only a few jars.
Gather many jars.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִ֨י שַׁאֲלִי־ לָ֤ךְ כֵּלִים֙ מִן־ הַח֔וּץ מֵאֵ֖ת כָּל־ שִׁכְנָכֵי כֵּלִ֥ים רֵקִ֖ים אַל־ תַּמְעִֽיטִי׃

passages.text: Then go inside, shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour oil into all these jars, setting the full ones aside.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
\r\nHe spoke to the woman and gave her instructions.
\r\nHe said, "Go into your house."
\r\nTake your sons with you.
\r\nShut the door behind you and your sons.
\r\nTake the jars you have gathered.
\r\nPour oil into all these jars.
\r\nWhen a jar is full, set it aside.
passages.original: וּבָ֗את וְסָגַ֤רְתְּ הַדֶּ֙לֶת֙ בַּעֲדֵ֣ךְ וּבְעַד־ בָּנַ֔יִךְ וְיָצַ֕קְתְּ עַ֥ל כָּל־ הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְהַמָּלֵ֖א תַּסִּֽיעִי׃

passages.text: So she left him, and after she had shut the door behind her and her sons, they kept bringing jars to her, and she kept pouring.
passages.sermon:
The woman left Elisha.
She shut the door behind herself and her sons.
Her sons brought jars to her.
She poured oil into the jars.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ מֵֽאִתּ֔וֹ וַתִּסְגֹּ֣ר הַדֶּ֔לֶת בַּעֲדָ֖הּ וּבְעַ֣ד בָּנֶ֑יהָ הֵ֛ם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים אֵלֶ֖יהָ וְהִ֥יא מֵיצָקֶת׃

passages.text: When all the jars were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another.” But he replied, “There are no more jars.” Then the oil stopped flowing.
passages.sermon:
A widow and her sons gathered many jars.
They filled every jar with oil.
All the jars became full.
The widow spoke to her son.
She said, “Bring me another jar.”
Her son answered her.
He said, “There are no more jars.”
The oil stopped flowing.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ כִּמְלֹ֣את הַכֵּלִ֗ים וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־ בְּנָהּ֙ הַגִּ֨ישָׁה אֵלַ֥י עוֹד֙ כֶּ֔לִי וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד כֶּ֑לִי וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: She went and told the man of God, and he said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt. Then you and your sons can live on the remainder.”
passages.sermon:
A widow had two sons.
She went to Elisha.
Elisha was a prophet and a man of God.
She told Elisha what had happened.
Elisha said, "Go."
"Sell the oil."
"Pay your debt."
"You and your sons can live on what is left."
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֗א וַתַּגֵּד֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִי֙ מִכְרִ֣י אֶת־ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶן וְשַׁלְּמִ֖י אֶת־ נִשְׁיֵכִי וְאַ֣תְּ בְּנֵיכִי תִֽחְיִ֖י בַּנּוֹתָֽר׃פ

passages.text: One day Elisha went to Shunem, and a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal. So whenever he would pass by, he would stop there to eat.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
One day Elisha traveled to the town of Shunem.
A prominent woman lived in Shunem.
This woman saw Elisha.
She persuaded Elisha to eat a meal with her.
After that, Elisha often passed through Shunem.
Whenever Elisha passed by, he would stop at her house.
He would eat a meal there.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אֶל־ שׁוּנֵ֗ם וְשָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַתַּחֲזֶק־ בּ֖וֹ לֶאֱכָל־ לָ֑חֶם וַֽיְהִי֙ מִדֵּ֣י עָבְר֔וֹ יָסֻ֥ר שָׁ֖מָּה לֶאֱכָל־ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: Then the woman said to her husband, “Behold, now I know that the one who often comes our way is a holy man of God.
passages.sermon:
A woman lived in Shunem.
She was a prominent woman.
She spoke to her husband.
She said, “Look, I know something now.
The man who often passes by us is a holy man.
He is a man of God.
He comes by our house regularly.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ אִישָׁ֔הּ הִנֵּה־ נָ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים קָד֣וֹשׁ ה֑וּא עֹבֵ֥ר עָלֵ֖ינוּ תָּמִֽיד׃

passages.text: Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him. Then when he comes to us, he can stay there.”
passages.sermon:
A prominent woman lived in Shunem.
She spoke to her husband.
She said, “Let us make a small room upstairs.
Let us put a bed in the room for Elisha.
Let us also put a table in the room.
Let us put a chair in the room.
Let us put a lamp in the room.
When Elisha comes to us, he can stay in that room.”
passages.original: נַֽעֲשֶׂה־ נָּ֤א עֲלִיַּת־ קִיר֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה וְנָשִׂ֨ים ל֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם מִטָּ֥ה וְשֻׁלְחָ֖ן וְכִסֵּ֣א וּמְנוֹרָ֑ה וְהָיָ֛ה בְּבֹא֥וֹ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ יָס֥וּר שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: One day Elisha came to visit and went to his upper room to lie down.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet and a holy man of God.
One day, Elisha came to visit the Shunammite family.
He went to the small upper room they had prepared for him.
Elisha lay down in that room.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם וַיָּ֣בֹא שָׁ֑מָּה וַיָּ֥סַר אֶל־ הָעֲלִיָּ֖ה וַיִּשְׁכַּב־ שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: And he said to Gehazi his servant, “Call the Shunammite woman.” And when he had called her, she stood before him, and Elisha said to Gehazi, “Now tell her, ‘Look, you have gone to all this trouble for us. What can we do for you? Can we speak on your behalf to the king or the commander of the army?’ ” “I have a home among my own people,” she replied.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Gehazi was Elisha’s servant.
A woman from Shunem had shown great kindness to Elisha and Gehazi.
Elisha spoke to Gehazi.
He said, “Call the Shunammite woman.”
Gehazi called the woman.
The woman came and stood before Elisha.
Elisha spoke to Gehazi again.
He said, “Tell her this message.”
He said, “You have gone to much trouble for us.”
He said, “What can we do for you?”
He said, “Should we speak to the king for you?”
He said, “Should we speak to the commander of the army for you?”
The woman answered.
She said, “I live among my own people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ גֵּחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ קְרָ֖א לַשּׁוּנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את וַיִּקְרָא־ לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽיו׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אֱמָר־ נָ֣א אֵלֶיהָ֮ הִנֵּ֣ה חָרַ֣דְתְּ׀ אֵלֵינוּ֮ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַחֲרָדָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֒ מֶ֚ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֔ךְ הֲיֵ֤שׁ לְדַבֶּר־ לָךְ֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ א֖וֹ אֶל־ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֑א וַתֹּ֕אמֶר בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמִּ֖י אָנֹכִ֥י יֹשָֽׁבֶת׃

passages.text: So he asked, “Then what should be done for her?” “Well, she has no son,” Gehazi replied, “and her husband is old.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha wanted to help the Shunammite woman.
Elisha asked, “What should we do for her?”
Gehazi was Elisha’s servant.
Gehazi answered Elisha.
Gehazi said, “She has no son.”
Gehazi also said, “Her husband is old.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר וּמֶ֖ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י אֲבָ֛ל בֵּ֥ן אֵֽין־ לָ֖הּ וְאִישָׁ֥הּ זָקֵֽן׃

passages.text: “Call her,” said Elisha. So Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
\r\nElisha spoke to Gehazi.
\r\nGehazi was Elisha’s servant.
\r\nElisha said, “Call her.”
\r\nElisha meant the Shunammite woman.
\r\nGehazi called the Shunammite woman.
\r\nThe Shunammite woman came.
\r\nShe stood in the doorway.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר קְרָא־ לָ֑הּ וַיִּקְרָא־ לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד בַּפָּֽתַח׃

passages.text: And Elisha declared, “At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms.” “No, my lord,” she said. “Do not lie to your maidservant, O man of God.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha spoke to the woman.
Elisha said, “At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms.”
The woman answered Elisha.
She said, “No, my lord.”
She called Elisha a man of God.
She said, “Do not lie to your maidservant.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אַתִּי חֹבֶ֣קֶת בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־ אֲדֹנִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אַל־ תְּכַזֵּ֖ב בְּשִׁפְחָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But the woman did conceive, and at that time the next year she gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had told her.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha spoke to the woman.
Elisha told her she would have a son at the same time next year.
The woman became pregnant.
The next year, at that same time, she gave birth to a son.
This happened just as Elisha had said.
passages.original: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

passages.text: And the child grew, and one day he went out to his father, who was with the harvesters.
passages.sermon:
The child grew.
One day, the child went out.
The child went to his father.
His father was with the harvesters.
passages.original: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הַיָּ֑לֶד וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֶל־ אָבִ֖יו אֶל־ הַקֹּצְרִֽים׃

passages.text: “My head! My head!” he complained to his father. So his father told a servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
passages.sermon:
A young boy spoke to his father.
He said, “My head! My head!”
The boy complained about pain in his head.
The father spoke to a servant.
He said, “Carry him to his mother.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל־ אָבִ֖יו רֹאשִׁ֣י׀ רֹאשִׁ֑י וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ הַנַּ֔עַר שָׂאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־ אִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: After the servant had picked him up and carried him to his mother, the boy sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
passages.sermon:
A servant picked up the boy.
The servant carried the boy to his mother.
The boy sat on his mother’s lap.
He stayed there until noon.
The boy died.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂאֵ֔הוּ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־ אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב עַל־ בִּרְכֶּ֛יהָ עַד־ הַֽצָּהֳרַ֖יִם וַיָּמֹֽת׃

passages.text: And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God. Then she shut the door and went out.
passages.sermon:
The woman was the boy’s mother.
Her son had just died.
She went upstairs.
She carried her son with her.
She laid her son on the bed.
This bed belonged to the man of God.
She shut the door behind her.
She left the room.
passages.original: וַתַּ֙עַל֙ וַתַּשְׁכִּבֵ֔הוּ עַל־ מִטַּ֖ת אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא׃

passages.text: And the woman called her husband and said, “Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, that I may go quickly to the man of God and return.”
passages.sermon:
A woman’s son died suddenly.
She called to her husband.
She spoke to him.
She said, “Please send me one servant.
Please send me one donkey.
I will go quickly to the man of God.
I will return.”
passages.original: וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל־ אִישָׁהּ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁלְחָ֨ה נָ֥א לִי֙ אֶחָ֣ד מִן־ הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְאַחַ֖ת הָאֲתֹנ֑וֹת וְאָר֛וּצָה עַד־ אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאָשֽׁוּבָה׃

passages.text: “Why would you go to him today?” he replied. “It is not a New Moon or a Sabbath.” “Everything is all right,” she said.
passages.sermon:
The woman's husband spoke to her.
He asked her a question.
He said, "Why are you going to the man of God today?"
He said, "Today is not a New Moon."
He said, "Today is not a Sabbath."
She answered him.
She said, "Everything is all right."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַ֠דּוּעַ אַתִּי הֹלַכְתִּי אֵלָיו֙ הַיּ֔וֹם לֹֽא־ חֹ֖דֶשׁ וְלֹ֣א שַׁבָּ֑ת וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then she saddled the donkey and told her servant, “Drive onward; do not slow the pace for me unless I tell you.”
passages.sermon:
The Shunammite woman acted quickly.
She saddled the donkey herself.
She spoke to her servant.
She said, “Lead on and go forward.”
She told him, “Do not slow down for me.”
She added, “Only stop if I tell you.”
passages.original: וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֶֽל־ נַעֲרָ֖הּ נְהַ֣ג וָלֵ֑ךְ אַל־ תַּעֲצָר־ לִ֣י לִרְכֹּ֔ב כִּ֖י אִם־ אָמַ֥רְתִּי לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: So she set out and went to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her at a distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, there is the Shunammite woman.
passages.sermon:
The Shunammite woman left her home.
She traveled to Mount Carmel.
She went to see the man of God.
The man of God was Elisha.
Elisha saw the woman coming from far away.
Elisha spoke to his servant Gehazi.
Elisha said, “Look, there is the Shunammite woman.”
passages.original: וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ וַתָּב֛וֹא אֶל־ אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וַ֠יְהִי כִּרְא֨וֹת אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים אֹתָהּ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ גֵּיחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ הִנֵּ֖ה הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֥ית הַלָּֽז׃

passages.text: Please run out now to meet her and ask, ‘Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is your child all right?’ ” And she answered, “Everything is all right.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
\r\nHe saw the Shunammite woman coming from a distance.
\r\nElisha spoke to his servant Gehazi.
\r\nHe said, “Run now to meet her.”
\r\nHe told Gehazi to ask her three questions.
\r\nHe said, “Are you all right?”
\r\nHe said, “Is your husband all right?”
\r\nHe said, “Is your child all right?”
\r\nGehazi went and asked her these questions.
\r\nThe Shunammite woman answered him.
\r\nShe said, “Everything is all right.”
passages.original: עַתָּה֮ רֽוּץ־ נָ֣א לִקְרָאתָהּ֒ וֶאֱמָר־ לָ֗הּ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לָ֛ךְ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לְאִישֵׁ֖ךְ הֲשָׁל֣וֹם לַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: When she reached the man of God at the mountain, she clung to his feet. Gehazi came over to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her soul is in deep distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
passages.sermon:
The Shunammite woman came to the man of God at the mountain.
She held tightly to his feet.
Gehazi approached to push her away.
The man of God spoke to Gehazi.
He said, “Let her be.
She is deeply troubled in her soul.
The LORD has hidden the reason from me.
The LORD has not told me.”
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֞א אֶל־ אִ֤ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־ הָהָ֔ר וַֽתַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ גֵּֽיחֲזִ֜י לְהָדְפָ֗הּ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים הַרְפֵּֽה־ לָהּ֙ כִּֽי־ נַפְשָׁ֣הּ מָֽרָה־ לָ֔הּ וַֽיהוָה֙ הֶעְלִ֣ים מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְלֹ֥א הִגִּ֖יד לִֽי׃

passages.text: Then she said, “Did I ask you for a son, my lord? Didn’t I say, ‘Do not deceive me?’ ”
passages.sermon: The woman spoke to Elisha, the man of God.\r\nShe said, “I did not ask you for a son, my lord.\r\nI said, ‘Do not deceive me.’”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הֲשָׁאַ֥לְתִּי בֵ֖ן מֵאֵ֣ת אֲדֹנִ֑י הֲלֹ֣א אָמַ֔רְתִּי לֹ֥א תַשְׁלֶ֖ה אֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: So Elisha said to Gehazi, “Tie up your garment, take my staff in your hand, and go! If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. Then lay my staff on the boy’s face.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
\r\nGehazi was Elisha’s servant.
\r\nElisha spoke to Gehazi.
\r\nElisha said, “Tie up your garment.”
\r\nElisha said, “Take my staff in your hand.”
\r\nElisha said, “Go.”
\r\nElisha said, “If you meet anyone, do not greet him.”
\r\nElisha said, “If anyone greets you, do not answer him.”
\r\nElisha said, “Lay my staff on the boy’s face.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לְגֵיחֲזִ֜י חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ וְקַ֨ח מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֮ וָלֵךְ֒ כִּֽי־ תִמְצָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א תְבָרְכֶ֔נּוּ וְכִֽי־ יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א תַעֲנֶנּ֑וּ וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֖י עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַנָּֽעַר׃

passages.text: And the mother of the boy said, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So he got up and followed her.
passages.sermon:
The boy’s mother spoke.
She said, “The LORD lives.”
She said, “You also live.”
She said, “I will not leave you.”
Elisha got up.
Elisha followed her.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ם הַנַּ֔עַר חַי־ יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־ נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־ אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boy’s face, but there was no sound or response. So he went back to meet Elisha and told him, “The boy has not awakened.”
passages.sermon:
Gehazi was Elisha’s servant.
Gehazi went ahead of Elisha and the boy’s mother.
Gehazi took Elisha’s staff.
Gehazi laid the staff on the boy’s face.
The boy did not make a sound.
The boy did not respond.
Gehazi returned to Elisha.
Gehazi met Elisha.
Gehazi said to Elisha, “The boy has not awakened.”
passages.original: וְגֵחֲזִ֞י עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֶת־ הַמִּשְׁעֶ֙נֶת֙ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַנַּ֔עַר וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין קָ֑שֶׁב וַיָּ֤שָׁב לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיַּגֶּד־ ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א הֵקִ֖יץ הַנָּֽעַר׃

passages.text: When Elisha reached the house, there was the boy lying dead on his bed.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha came to the house.
He saw the boy.
The boy was dead.
The boy was lying on his bed.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֱלִישָׁ֖ע הַבָּ֑יְתָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַנַּ֙עַר֙ מֵ֔ת מֻשְׁכָּ֖ב עַל־ מִטָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So he went in, closed the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
\r\nElisha entered the house.
\r\nElisha and the dead boy were in the room.
\r\nElisha closed the door behind them.
\r\nElisha prayed to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר הַדֶּ֖לֶת בְּעַ֣ד שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Elisha got on the bed and lay on the boy, mouth to mouth, eye to eye, and hand to hand. As he stretched himself out over him, the boy’s body became warm.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha entered the room where the dead boy lay on the bed.
Elisha climbed onto the bed.
Elisha lay on top of the boy.
Elisha put his mouth on the boy’s mouth.
Elisha put his eyes on the boy’s eyes.
Elisha put his hands on the boy’s hands.
Elisha stretched himself out over the boy.
The boy’s body became warm.
passages.original: וַיַּ֜עַל וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עַל־ הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַיָּשֶׂם֩ פִּ֨יו עַל־ פִּ֜יו וְעֵינָ֤יו עַל־ עֵינָיו֙ וְכַפָּ֣יו עַל־ כַּפּוֹ וַיִּגְהַ֖ר עָלָ֑יו וַיָּ֖חָם בְּשַׂ֥ר הַיָּֽלֶד׃

passages.text: Elisha turned away and paced back and forth across the room. Then he got on the bed and stretched himself out over the boy again, and the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha turned away from the boy.
Elisha walked back and forth in the house.
Elisha went up to the bed again.
Elisha stretched himself out over the boy again.
The boy sneezed seven times.
The boy opened his eyes.
passages.original: וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּבַּ֗יִת אַחַ֥ת הֵ֙נָּה֙ וְאַחַ֣ת הֵ֔נָּה וַיַּ֖עַל וַיִּגְהַ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וַיְזוֹרֵ֤ר הַנַּ֙עַר֙ עַד־ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים וַיִּפְקַ֥ח הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת־ עֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: Elisha summoned Gehazi and said, “Call the Shunammite woman.” So he called her and she came. Then Elisha said, “Pick up your son.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
\r\nGehazi was Elisha’s servant.
\r\nThe Shunammite woman was the boy’s mother.
\r\nElisha called to Gehazi.
\r\nElisha said, “Call the Shunammite woman.”
\r\nGehazi called the woman.
\r\nThe woman came to Elisha.
\r\nElisha said, “Pick up your son.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֶל־ גֵּיחֲזִ֗י וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ קְרָא֙ אֶל־ הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וַיִּקְרָאֶ֖הָ וַתָּב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שְׂאִ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.
passages.sermon:
The Shunammite woman entered the room.
She saw Elisha.
She fell at Elisha’s feet.
She bowed down to the ground before him.
She picked up her son.
She left the room.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹא֙ וַתִּפֹּ֣ל עַל־ רַגְלָ֔יו וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָ֑רְצָה וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־ בְּנָ֖הּ וַתֵּצֵֽא׃פ

passages.text: When Elisha returned to Gilgal, there was a famine in the land. As the sons of the prophets were sitting at his feet, he said to his attendant, “Put on the large pot and boil some stew for the sons of the prophets.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha returned to Gilgal.
There was a famine in the land.
The sons of the prophets sat before Elisha.
Elisha spoke to his attendant.
He said, “Put on the large pot.”
He said, “Boil some stew for the sons of the prophets.”
passages.original: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֙לָה֙ וְהָרָעָ֣ב בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּבְנֵי֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים יֹשְׁבִ֖ים לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְנַעֲר֗וֹ שְׁפֹת֙ הַסִּ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וּבַשֵּׁ֥ל נָזִ֖יד לִבְנֵ֥י הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃

passages.text: One of them went out to the field to gather herbs, and he found a wild vine from which he gathered as many wild gourds as his garment could hold. Then he came back and cut them up into the pot of stew, though no one knew what they were.
passages.sermon:
One man went out to the field.
He went to gather herbs.
He found a wild vine in the field.
He gathered wild gourds from the vine.
He filled his garment with the wild gourds.
He returned with the gourds.
He cut up the gourds.
He put the pieces into the pot of stew.
No one knew what the gourds were.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֨א אֶחָ֣ד אֶל־ הַשָּׂדֶה֮ לְלַקֵּ֣ט אֹרֹת֒ וַיִּמְצָא֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שָׂדֶ֔ה וַיְלַקֵּ֥ט מִמֶּ֛נּוּ פַּקֻּעֹ֥ת שָׂדֶ֖ה מְלֹ֣א בִגְד֑וֹ וַיָּבֹ֗א וַיְפַלַּ֛ח אֶל־ סִ֥יר הַנָּזִ֖יד כִּֽי־ לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: And they poured it out for the men to eat, but when they tasted the stew they cried out, “There is death in the pot, O man of God!” And they could not eat it.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
There was a famine in the land.
The sons of the prophets sat before Elisha.
They poured out the stew for the men to eat.
The men began to eat the stew.
They tasted the stew.
They cried out loudly.
They said, “There is death in the pot, O man of God!”
They could not eat the stew.
passages.original: וַיִּֽצְק֥וּ לַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וַ֠יְהִי כְּאָכְלָ֨ם מֵהַנָּזִ֜יד וְהֵ֣מָּה צָעָ֗קוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מָ֤וֶת בַּסִּיר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ לֶאֱכֹֽל׃

passages.text: Then Elisha said, “Get some flour.” He threw it into the pot and said, “Pour it out for the people to eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha saw that the stew was dangerous.
Elisha said, “Get some flour.”
Elisha took the flour.
Elisha threw the flour into the pot.
Elisha said, “Pour the stew out for the people to eat.”
The people ate the stew.
There was nothing harmful in the pot.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ וּקְחוּ־ קֶ֔מַח וַיַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־ הַסִּ֑יר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר צַ֤ק לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה דָּבָ֥ר רָ֖ע בַּסִּֽיר׃ס

passages.text: Now a man from Baal-shalishah came to the man of God with a sack of twenty loaves of barley bread from the first ripe grain. “Give it to the people to eat,” said Elisha.
passages.sermon:
A man came from Baal-shalishah.
He brought bread to the man of God.
He brought twenty loaves of barley bread.
He brought bread made from the first ripe grain.
He carried the bread in a sack.
Elisha was the man of God.
Elisha said, “Give it to the people to eat.”
passages.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לֶ֤חֶם בִּכּוּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִֽים־ לֶ֣חֶם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים וְכַרְמֶ֖ל בְּצִקְלֹנ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר תֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וְיֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: But his servant asked, “How am I to set twenty loaves before a hundred men?” “Give it to the people to eat,” said Elisha, “for this is what the LORD says: ‘They will eat and have some left over.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
A man brought Elisha twenty loaves of barley bread.
There were one hundred men to feed.
Elisha’s servant spoke to him.
The servant said, “How can I give this to one hundred men?”
Elisha answered his servant.
Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they may eat.”
Elisha said, “The LORD says they will eat and have some left over.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ מָ֚ה אֶתֵּ֣ן זֶ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י מֵ֣אָה אִ֑ישׁ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תֵּ֤ן לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָכֹ֥ל וְהוֹתֵֽר׃

passages.text: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The servant placed the food in front of the people.
The people ate the food.
They had food left over.
This happened as the LORD had said.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֛ם וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ וַיּוֹתִ֖רוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃פ
